$comment: D-MIR-SYNTHESIZED-SYMBOL-MINTED-INSIDE-THE-NAME-TABLE (P69 round 5, lane lm): a two-unit program whose RELEASE build makes a zero constant in a unit where a number counted from the module's own symbols is the id of a block-scope extern. C defines the result (x is assigned on the path taken): 42. MEASURED 2026-10-08 ON THE REFERENCES (probe-reference-cc, the two files as they are here): 42 at -O0, -O1, -O2, -O3 and -Os from gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 on x86_64 Linux (run 20261008-145211-8c845c0a), gcc 13.3.0 on aarch64 Linux (20261008-145235-184527d2), Apple clang 21 on arm64 (20261008-145256-c2ad4ac8) and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0, and at /Od, /O1, /O2 and /Ox from cl (20261008-145314-62d34279). MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX, this example in both runners (run 20261008-140243-ebaccdc0 on Windows and Linux, 20261008-144535-97abe506 on the Mac): the debug arm returned 42 on every target, and the RELEASE arm built with no diagnostic and DIED on every one -- pe64 0xC0000005, x86_64 ELF signal 11, aarch64 ELF (qemu) exit 132, Mach-O arm64 and x86_64 signal 4: the optimizer's zero constant had taken the id of `ext_in`'s import, so one SymbolId named a constant and a function at once. Since round 5 the MODULE hands out the id (`MirBuilder::mintSymbol`), past the name table and every import. RED-ON-DISABLE: make mem2reg count the id from the module's functions and globals again -> the release arm dies as measured.
